To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

O 3-induced leaf injury and ethylene synthesis were inhibited by 1-MCP treatment in tobacco. 1-MCP did not affect the accumulation of salicylic acid, but it suppressed the expression of genes that were induced by O 3.
O 3-induced gene expression is mediated through the synthesis of SA and that the O 3-induced SA synthesis is mediated through ethylene production.
the O3-induced gene expression and ethylene production are enhanced by the presence of the NO donor, and that the NO donor enhances the O3-induced leaf injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ozone exposure on the physiology and biochemistry of plants.
the development of a new class of compounds that can inhibit the activity of the enzymes involved in ethylene synthesis and thus reduce ethylene production and ethylene action.
the effects of ozone on the growth, physiology and metabolism of plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ozone exposure of the tobacco plants caused a significant reduction in the growth rate and the biomass production of the tobacco plants, but the reduction was not due to the ozone-induced oxidative stress.

the ozone exposure and the resulting injury to the leaf is the result of a complex interaction of the plant's genetic and physiological response to ozone and the environment in which the plant is growing.
ozone exposure causes oxidative stress and that the resulting ROS production is a primary cause of ozone injury in sensitive plants, but that ozone-induced ROS are not the sole cause of ozone injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the O 3-induced expression of genes involved in the biosynthesis of ethylene, salicylic acid, and jasmonic acid is regulated by the transcription factor ORE1 in tobacco.

the ozone ( O3 )-induced leaf injury in tobacco plants is caused by the activation of the ethylene biosynthetic and signaling pathway, the activation of salicylic acid synthesis, and the induction of O 3-responsive genes.

ozone is a very important air pollutant that can have a negative effect on the growth and development of plants, and that this effect can be mitigated through the use of ozone-tolerant cultivars and/or by applying ozone-protecting compounds to plants.

O 3 can induce the production of ethylene, a potent signaling molecule, in plants, which in turn activates the expression of genes involved in the synthesis of salicylic acid (SA) and other signaling molecules.
